::: {#exm-racket-properties}
#### Checking properties in Racket

The predicate `related?` turns the answer of `member` into `#t` or `#f`:

```racket
(define (related? R a b)
  (if (member (list a b) R) #t #f))
```

`(for/and ([x L]) body)` evaluates `body` once for each element `x` of the list `L`,
and returns `#f` as soon as `body` returns `#f`, and `#t` if it never does.
`for*/and`, which @rem-racket-equivalence uses to go through the rows of a truth table,
does the same for every combination of values of its variables,
here every two pairs of a relation:

```racket
(define (reflexive? S R)
  (for/and ([a S])
    (related? R a a)))

(define (symmetric? R)
  (for/and ([p R])
    (related? R (second p) (first p))))

(define (transitive? R)
  (for*/and ([p R]
             [q R])
    (or (not (equal? (second p) (first q)))
        (related? R (first p) (second q)))))
```

- `reflexive?` checks $a \mathrel{R} a$ for each element $a$ of the set `S` (@def-reflexive).
  It needs `S`, because the list `R` says nothing about an element that is in no pair.
- `symmetric?` checks, for each pair $(a, b)$ in `R`, that $(b, a)$ is in `R` too (@def-symmetric-relation).
- `transitive?` checks, for every two pairs $(a, b)$ and $(b', c)$ of `R`, the conditional
  "if $b = b'$, then $a \mathrel{R} c$" (@def-transitive),
  written as an `or` by @cor-conditional-as-or.

All three of `(reflexive? (list 'rock 'paper 'scissors) beats)`, `(symmetric? beats)` and `(transitive? beats)` return `#f`,
as @exm-reflexive-or-not, @exm-symmetric-or-not and @exm-transitive-or-not found.

:::
